caveats:
The spatial accuracy of the health facilities dataset depends on both the quality of the input data and the correctness of edits applied throughout the validation process. Temporal mismatches may exist between the point datasets and the satellite imagery used for quality checks. These discrepancies may result in health facilities not being identified or in the inclusion of facilities that are no longer operational. Spelling errors and naming inconsistencies may also occur due to colloquial variations in how locations are referenced in the field.

Significant gaps remain in the spatial coverage of health facilities in the DRC. In Kongo Central Province, geolocation data are available for fewer than 40% of the facilities listed in the DHIS2 database. In Kwango (Boko, Kenge, and Kimbao), Haut-Uele, Bas-Uele, Nord-Kivu or Sud-Kivu Provinces no new field data collection was conducted, therefore health facility records for these provinces rely on data collected as far back as 2018, which may no longer reflect current conditions. Users are advised to apply caution when working with these features. 

This dataset should be considered operational; it has not been fully validated by government authorities. Its production is part of ongoing work, and additional edits and refinements are expected in future releases.

CIESIN, Columbia University, and its co-authors follow procedures designed to ensure that data disseminated by the project are of reasonable quality. If, despite these procedures, users encounter apparent errors or misstatements in the data, they should contact CIESIN, info@ciesin.columbia.edu.

CIESIN, Columbia University, its co-authors, and their sponsors do not guarantee the accuracy, reliability, or completeness of any data provided. notes:
The GRID3 COD - Health Facilities v9.0 dataset consists of health facility points with name, location, health zone, and health area, among other attributes, for all the twenty-six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (COD).

The current version supersedes the GRID3 COD - Health Facilities v8.0 <https://data.grid3.org/datasets/GRID3::grid3-cod-health-facilities-v8-0/about>. The following changes were made:

Health facility points added.
Corrections to health facility names.

organization.description:
GRID3 works with countries in sub-Saharan Africa to generate, validate, and use core spatial datasets on population, settlements, subnational boundaries, and crucial infrastructure. We train and support stakeholders who use this information for analytics and decision-making, and work closely with local governments to improve national ownership and sustainability of the data.

We blend official data with data generated by novel approaches; our solutions draw on advanced data science and technology, participatory mapping, satellite imagery, and other innovations. GRID3 combines the expertise of leading technical partners to design pragmatic and responsive geospatial solutions that address the priority needs of each country.

Our work facilitates data-driven interventions that reach communities that need them the most. GRID3 solutions are valuable across multiple development sectors, from education to infrastructure. Our current focus is improving health interventions—particularly immunization coverage and malaria control—in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Nigeria.
